events.summary:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 800 PM MDT.

* At 256 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons, normally
dry washes, creeks, streams and rivers. Hole- in-the-Rock
Road may be impassible in areas that receive heavy rain.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Croton Canyon, Coyote Gulch, Brimstone, Peekaboo, Forty Mile Gulch,
Fifty Mile Gulch, Davis Gulch and other drainages on
Hole-in-the-Rock Road.

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Englewood to Tarpon Springs FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Tarpon Springs to Suwannee River FL out 20
NM...
Tampa Bay waters...

* Until 600 PM EDT.

extending from 11 nm northeast of Howard Frankland Bridge to near
Courtney Campbell Causeway to near Longboat Pass, moving northwest

all on board are wearing life jackets.

Madeira Beach Reef, Longboat Key, Tierra Verde, Belleair Beach,
Cockroach Bay, M7 Reef, Anna Maria Island, Saint Armands Key, M8
Reef, Pass-A-Grille Channel, Southwest Channel, M1 Reef, Tampa Bay,
St. Pete Beach, Hillsborough Bay, Bradenton Beach, and Honeymoon
Island.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 241 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 0.75 and 1.3 inches of rain have fallen on the northeast
slopes of Magdalena Mountain.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Socorro County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Antelope Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 500 PM MST /600 PM MDT/.

* At 133 PM MST /233 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the Antelope Creek basin. Between 0.5 and
1 inch of rain has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to
0.75 inches are possible with approaching storms in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Antelope Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Antelope Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rattlesnake Canyon, Owl Canyon, Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower
Antelope Canyon, Porcupine Canyon, Mountain Sheep Canyon, LeChee
and Wind Pebble Canyon.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon, Rattlesnake
Canyon and Porcupine Canyon.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Antelope Creek.
